claims.text: CodePipeline's default execution mode is SUPERSEDED.
In CodePipeline's SUPERSEDED execution mode, a stage is locked to one execution at a time.
In CodePipeline SUPERSEDED mode, a newer execution can overtake an execution that is waiting to enter a locked stage, dropping the waiting execution before it starts.
In SUPERSEDED mode, a queued execution waiting behind a CodeBuild stage running `pulumi up` can be superseded and never run, silently skipping a deployment.
Setting CodePipeline's execution mode to QUEUED makes waiting executions form a queue and each run in turn.
CodePipeline's QUEUED execution mode requires a V2 pipeline type.
The AWS CLI's create-pipeline and update-pipeline commands accept executionMode and pipelineType settings in the pipeline definition.
The aws.codepipeline.Pipeline resource in the Pulumi AWS provider has `executionMode` and `pipelineType` inputs.
Cross-references: link to AWS CodePipeline concepts page and the Pulumi registry aws.codepipeline.Pipeline API docs page exist.
When two runs reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them, and the other's `pulumi up` fails with an update conflict.
Azure Pipelines supports an exclusive lock check on an environment, which can prevent concurrent runs from deploying to the environment targeted by a deployment job.
The exclusive lock check is added from the environment's 'Approvals and checks' tab in Azure DevOps.
In Azure Pipelines YAML, `lockBehavior` is set at the stage level to control exclusive lock behavior for the stage referencing the environment.
The default value of Azure Pipelines `lockBehavior` is `runLatest`.
With `lockBehavior: runLatest`, only the most recently queued run acquires the exclusive lock, and older runs waiting behind it are passed over (canceled) rather than eventually applied.
With `lockBehavior: sequential`, every queued stage run acquires the exclusive lock in order, one at a time.
Pulumi Cloud serializes updates to a stack one at a time, in order, in the same way as `sequential` lock behavior.
The Azure DevOps provider in the Pulumi Registry has a `azuredevops.CheckExclusiveLock` resource that manages the exclusive lock check as code.
The Pulumi@1 Azure Pipelines task accepts inputs `command: up`, `stack`, and `args`.
Links to the update-conflicts troubleshooting page and the registry checkexclusivelock api-docs page must exist.

When two runs of the same TeamCity build configuration reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one, and the other's `pulumi up` fails with an update conflict.
TeamCity's default is to let build configurations run concurrently against as many free agents as are available.
The link /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ exists as a page documenting update conflicts.
TeamCity build configurations have an advanced option named "Limit the number of simultaneously running builds" under the configuration's General Settings.
The TeamCity option "Limit the number of simultaneously running builds" defaults to 0, meaning unlimited.
Setting TeamCity's "Limit the number of simultaneously running builds" to 1 queues a second build behind the first, running only after the first finishes.
Pulumi Cloud has a per-stack lease that gives one-at-a-time update behavior.
In Azure Pipelines, adding an exclusive lock check to the environment targeted by the deployment job serializes deployments to that environment.
In Azure Pipelines, the stage-level setting `lockBehavior: sequential` is used together with an exclusive lock check so runs proceed sequentially.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/azure-devops/ has a section 'serialize-deployments-with-an-exclusive-lock'.
In AWS CodePipeline, setting the pipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions run in turn.
AWS CodePipeline's default execution mode (SUPERSEDED) lets a newer execution supersede an older one that is still waiting to start.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/aws-code-services/ has a section 'serialize-pipeline-executions'.
In TeamCity, the build configuration setting 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' set to 1 serializes builds.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/teamcity/ has a section 'limit-concurrent-builds'.
